claim: Let \(\alpha>0\), and let \(A\) be an inverse \(M\)-matrix of order at most \(3\). Then the set function \(S\mapsto\operatorname{per}_{\alpha}(A_S)\) is log-supermodular. In order \(3\), after relabeling the only nontrivial overlapping incomparable case has \(S=\{1,2\}\), \(T=\{2,3\}\); writing \(A=\begin{pmatrix}a&u&r\\v&b&p\\s&q&c\end{pmatrix}\), its defect equals \(\alpha^2[\alpha b^2rs+bups+qv(br-up)]\ge0\), because \(A\ge0\) and \((A^{-1})_{13}=(up-br)/\det A\le0\). Thus the conclusion includes nonsymmetrizable inverse \(M\)-matrices and holds for every \(\alpha>0\). Dimension \(3\) is maximal for a statement uniform in both \(\alpha>0\) and all inverse \(M\)-matrices, since the four-vertex family in Sra's Appendix A fails log-supermodularity for sufficiently small positive parameters whenever \(\alpha<(\sqrt5-1)/2\).

correctness.rationale: For order \(3\), all set pairs reduce to nested, disjoint, or one overlapping incomparable pattern. Disjoint pairs are handled by nonnegative cross-block permutation terms. The remaining defect expands exactly to \(\alpha^2[\alpha b^2rs+bups+qv(br-up)]\), and the inverse \(M\)-matrix cofactor sign gives \(br-up\ge0\). The proof therefore covers every positive \(\alpha\) without relying on finite enumeration. The standalone exact checker independently reconstructs the polynomial identity and a nonsymmetrizable example.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact boundary result directly motivated by Sra's fixed-dimension open problem. It fully resolves \(n\le3\) for every positive \(\alpha\), identifies the first dimension where a uniform-all-\(\alpha\) theorem can fail, and adds genuinely nonsymmetrizable coverage beyond the existing structural positive cases. The result is compact but mathematically structural rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
